articles.title: Why isn't alcohol seen as a public health emergency?
articles.summary_4_sentences: This article asks why alcohol is not treated as a public health emergency. The framing suggests a mismatch between alcohol-related harm and policy urgency. It appears to be part of a broader series on alcohol's toll. The piece pushes readers to reconsider how society categorizes major health threats.

Even so, the article says some observers are worried about policy shifts and changes in the drug supply. The piece balances encouraging mortality data with caution about future reversals. It highlights the fragility of progress in the overdose crisis.

articles.title: STAT Plus: Alcohol is wreaking havoc on U.S. public health. American society looks the other way
articles.summary_4_sentences: This article argues that alcohol is causing major public health harm in the U.S. while receiving insufficient attention. It appears to be the opening installment of a broader series. The framing emphasizes normalization and neglect rather than lack of evidence. The piece sets up alcohol as an underrecognized driver of illness and death.

articles.title: PCOS's new name is PMOS, a small letter change that required a big scientific process
articles.summary_4_sentences: PCOS has been renamed PMOS after what the article describes as a substantial scientific process. The change appears small in wording but significant in meaning. The new name likely aims to better reflect the condition's biology and clinical scope. The story shows how disease terminology can influence understanding and care.

articles.title: STAT Plus: Ambiguous loss: a peculiar kind of grief in dementia care
articles.summary_4_sentences: This article explores ambiguous loss in the context of dementia care. It focuses on the distinctive grief experienced in relationships and marriage when a loved one changes but remains physically present. The piece brings attention to an emotional dimension of caregiving that is often hard to name. It broadens the conversation about dementia beyond clinical symptoms alone.
